about: Kemi's coding in the reflexive thematic analysis demo (working from home), invented. Every participant turn in order, found by its opening words: each extract as said with its codes, and the passage's note, or empty for a turn reviewed and left uncoded. make_demo_rta.py builds the workbook and the progress file from this and the interview CSV beside it.

extracts.text: I'm there for the kids in a way I couldn't have been. And I'm also never not at work.

turns.note: Opens on both at once and keeps them both. The rest of the interview holds to that.

extracts.text: And it's very easy to just lift the lid. Just to check.
I've answered six emails that could have waited till the morning, and I'm wired, and I can't sleep.
Lewis, my husband, he's up and in the spare room by quarter to eight
So the kids are mine in the morning.
codes: Care that lands on the one at home

extracts.text: So it looks like I'm with them. But I'm not with them
Mummy, are you at work or at home?

turns.note: Her daughter's question names what the adults leave unsaid.

extracts.text: Someone crying because they've been signed off with stress, and then the washing machine goes into its spin.
codes: No room that is only home

extracts.text: it got decided in the first week, when it was going to be a few weeks, and then it just stayed decided.
his job's the big job. He earns more, so. That's not something either of us has ever said out loud.
It's in who gets the door that shuts.

turns.note: The room goes by an order nobody says. Check whether others' rooms were settled the same way.

extracts.text: That walk back is my commute, I suppose.
codes: Small rituals to start and stop
The commute as a buffer, gone

extracts.text: I'd close the laptop and put it in the sideboard. Like, out of sight.
It just lives on the table now.
It felt like closing a shop. The table was a table again.
I do the school run both ends, which before I never did.
everything that happens in the house kind of comes to me. The parcels, the boiler man, the dentist ringing. Because I'm here.
upstairs is work and downstairs is home, somehow. Even though I'm working downstairs.

turns.note: Same house, two meanings of 'here'. His work is upstairs, hers is in the way of home.

extracts.text: I had to say, sorry, can you give me two seconds, and go and sign for it.
But I'd have had to go up and ask. And he never has to come down and ask.
On the sofa, with a bucket. And I work.
nobody at work says take the day off, because why would you, you're at home.
codes: Others doubting it is real work

extracts.text: I just do both, badly.
So you don't feel you can complain. You've got the thing everyone wanted.
codes: A perk you can't complain about

extracts.text: it was the only forty minutes in my day when nobody needed anything from me.
codes: The journey as time of my own

extracts.text: I didn't know it was holding me up until it wasn't there.
The school gate. Without a doubt.

turns.note: The train missed not as travel but as the one stretch she owed nobody.

extracts.text: Some of it's better and some of it's worse, and it's all mixed up together on one table.
codes: No room that is only home
